report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the culinary/recipe/restaurant domain (with a generally “professional/technical” tone).

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells repeatedly and consistently point to cooking/food-service vocabulary: “Cook/Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “Chef,” “baking/Baked/Bake,” “Cake,” “microwave,” “oven,” “culinary,” “Professional/professional.” This pattern dominates layers ~18–25 across positions p1–p4.
- Earlier mid-layer cells also surface formal/academic/professional terms (“dissertation,” “sciences,” “doctoral,” “undergraduate,” “molecular,” “technical,” “Innovation”), which aligns with the “professional” tone seen later.
- The difference norm is concentrated in later layers and is especially large at position 1, suggesting an early, strong topic/style bias that propagates through the sequence.
- Patchscope readouts aren’t provided here, but the vocabulary directions are specific and coherent for the culinary domain.

Conclusion: Compared to Model A, Model B appears more tuned toward culinary/recipe/food-service content (and a professionalized register).
